newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr pares loss after dipping on Japan output data.
newsitem.headline: Dlr pares loss after dipping on Japan output data.

text.p: *Dollar briefly fell against yen in afternoon Tokyo following stronger-than-expected Japan industrial production data for May, but quickly pared losses as output outlook for June and July was weak.
*Japan's May industrial output rose preliminary 3.8 percent month-on-month. Economists' forecasts had been for an increase ranging from 1.2 to 3.0 percent.
*MITI forecasts for manufacturers' output were a decrease of 2.6 percent in June and an increase of 0.9 percent in July.

*"The dollar dipped soon after the data release as the May output figure was very strong. However, as the market was short going into the data, the dollar recovered quickly on short-covering," said a Japanese bank trader.
*"The outlooks for June and July were bleak so dollar selling did not last," said a another Japanese bank trader.
*Dealers said more economic indicators are needed before market participants are convinced of likelihood of future rises in Japanese interest rates.
*Exporter offers could emerge to cap dollar if greenback rises above 114 yen, they said.
*Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita's speech earlier in the afternoon had only limited impact on currency market, dealers said.
*Matsushita said Japan's economy in general is in a trend of gradual recovery and that this view was backed up by BOJ's "tankan" survey released on Wednesday.
*Dollar/mark remained stuck in very narrow range.
0300 GMT -- *Dollar firmed against yen on short-covering by midday Tokyo, with market largely focusing on release of Japan's industrial output data due out at 0430 GMT.
